description: Second consecutive failed attempt to fix the One Texas H1 2026 Scorecard slide layout. First pass deleted clutter without reflowing (err-20260730T160121-5S1CFZ). Second pass (sub-agent) claimed it resized/repositioned shapes to fill the slide and verified this programmatically via python-pptx bounding-box math, but David reports it is still not legible and still does not fill the slide. The sub-agent's 'verification' checked shape coordinates against slide bounds but evidently did not catch the actual visual/legibility problem (likely font/text-box proportions, real rendering vs. raw XML math, or an incorrect assumption about what 'filling the slide' should look like).
correction: Coordinate-math verification against python-pptx bounding boxes is not sufficient proof that a slide is visually correct. Before reporting a layout fix as complete, the actual rendered slide must be visually inspected (export to PDF/image and look at it) rather than trusting shape-position arithmetic alone.
systemic_fix: For any visual/layout task (slides, documents, images), require a render-and-look step as the final verification gate, not a data-level check. Master should do this inspection itself before relaying a sub-agent's 'verified' claim to David, rather than passing through unverified confidence a second time.
